Fee-simple default: a Surrey lot trades fee-simple unless its title says otherwise — no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees.

A name that surfaced inside listing text in Surrey home listings only, not verified on a developer, strata or manager source — queued, counted nowhere, in the townhomes assembly and here alike. items.t: In its own words: "Explore Surrey's official land use and community plans to understand where future growth, rezoning, and development are happening," across "Whalley, City Centre, Cloverdale, and surrounding areas."

Board geography: there is no board sub-area for this page's topic — the page covers the whole City of Surrey's secondary-plan system. Board-name positions: Surrey City Centre is not a board name — the land is the Whalley sub-area — while "City Centre" remains the City's own planning name for the downtown plan area, which is how the tile legitimately uses it; the intro's pairing of "Whalley, City Centre" reads as two peer areas, but for board purposes they are one.
Serpentine — dual filing stated, no market claim built on either: Serpentine is a Fraser Valley board sub-area (owner ruling, Nov 1, 2026). No Serpentine plan tile appears on this page.

How Surrey's plan system is organized (City's own land-use-planning pages): the City organizes its approved secondary plans by community — South Surrey, Newton, Cloverdale, Whalley, Guildford/Fleetwood among them — and describes approved plans as developed through community consultation and endorsed by Council, providing neighbourhood-level detail on land use designations and density, road networks, amenities and servicing. Plan types: the General Land Use Plan (GLUP, the overall framework), the Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP, the detailed neighbourhood plan under it) and the Local Area Plan (LAP).
How people search for it: "Surrey land use plans," "Surrey NCP," "Surrey community plans," "Clayton NCP," "Grandview Heights plans," "Surrey development plans map."

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Surrey

items.t: Zoning — Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000: (zone minimums read parcel by parcel in COSMOS). Streamside setbacks sit in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw 12000 and vary by stream class — no single riparian figure is ever stated for Surrey.

SSMUH — Surrey: the City adopted its provincial small-scale multi-unit housing zoning change on July 8, 2024, when Zoning By-law No. 12000's residential zones R1 to R7 replaced the RF, RH and RQ zones (RF-12/RF-12C became R4; RF-SD became R6) — the zoning now does the small-lot permitting that older NCP designations predate, so a plan tile and the current zone can point in different directions on the same lot.

Subdivision and servicing — Surrey Subdivision and Development (servicing) Bylaw, 1986, No. 8830, verified on the City's own pages (carried with that sourcing), through the City's Servicing Agreement process. A specific parcel's servicing position is per-parcel: Not verified until confirmed with the City. (Standing verified ledger.)

ALR block (where a Surrey parcel is ALR — status per-parcel, not verified here): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Check a parcel on the ALC maps.

items.t: For Grandview Heights lots, start from the GLUP, not the neighbourhood tile: the City's structure puts the Grandview Heights GLUP over the individual NCPs (Darts Hill, Morgan Heights, North Grandview Heights, Orchard Grove, Redwood Heights, Sunnyside Heights).

The South Westminster tile is behind the City's current position (Mar 10, 2025). The City records that on March 10, 2025 Council endorsed Corporate Report R048, concluding the plan update for the predominantly industrial and employment portion of the South Westminster plan area and identifying a Waterfront District Study Area and a Transit Village Study Area at Scott Road Station for future planning — the tile describes the original NCP area only.
The remaining tiles' details are not verified as stated (Nov 1, 2026).
The page carries no FAQ block, so there are no unanswered FAQ questions, and no open-house listings to conflict.

blocks.text: Surrey Lots and Land: streets and boundaries

items.t: This page is City of Surrey-wide land, and Surrey is its own municipality with its own zoning bylaw, separate from Langley Township to the east.
Surrey's land splits into upland lots and lowland floodplain: the Serpentine and Nicomekl lowlands cover 59 square kilometres (km²) of a 334 km² catchment, as the City states.
A land buyer's status check is the City's Online Development Inquiry, which needs the property address, development project number or building permit number.

blocks.text: Surrey Lots and Land: the housing stock

items.t: The land stock here is serviced urban lots, assembly parcels and rural Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) pockets under one city-wide search, not one subdivision.
Lot size drives the zone label after the 2024 rezoning: for example RA (Acreage Residential Zone) covers lots over 4,050 square metres (m²) in the City's small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) table.

blocks.text: Surrey Lots and Land: rules that affect buyers

items.t: 12000, amended for SSMUH on July 8, 2024.

The 2024 changes replaced older zones — RA became Acreage Residential, RH (Half-Acre) became R1 Suburban Residential, and RF/RF-SS became R3 Urban Residential — so an old zone name on a document must be translated.
Over 4,600 Comprehensive Development (CD) lots keep their site-specific CD regulations; added SSMUH permissions apply by lot size under Part 52 of the zoning bylaw.
Coach houses and garden suites are 35 m² minimum and 75 m² maximum, excluded from floor area ratio (FAR), rising to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots where the main house is below maximum FAR.
In the ALR, the Agricultural Land Commission caps a principal residence at 500 m² and requires a suite to be inside that residence.

blocks.text: Surrey Lots and Land: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: About 13,000 eligible Surrey lots (around 18% of SSMUH lots) sit within frequent bus stop areas with 15-minute service, where up to 6 units and no off-street parking may apply.
A coach house must be attached to a garage, and smaller R3–R6 lots need lane access for one; without a lane, a garden suite may be the route instead.
A coach house or garden suite needs one extra parking space beyond the spaces required for the house, duplex and any secondary suite.
SSMUH does not retroactively legalize a suite or coach house built without permits; owners must still go through permit and approval channels.

blocks.text: Surrey Lots and Land: development and new projects

items.t: Surrey Development Cost Charge Bylaw, 2025, No. 21598 is the active land-cost project: introduced March 10, 2025, revised after provincial review, and before Council on July 28, 2025 for filing, readings and submission for provincial approval before final adoption.
On July 27, 2026 Council approved a comprehensive review of SSMUH regulations and implementation, which can change what a Surrey lot may build.

blocks.text: Surrey Lots and Land: costs and taxes

items.t: Surrey's 2026 total residential (Class 1) tax rate is $3.42731 per $1,000 of assessed value, of which the Municipal Total is $1.84251 per $1,000.

Farm (Class 9) is taxed differently in the same 2026 schedule: Municipal Total $4.48750 per $1,000 and Total tax rate $12.57740 per $1,000 — a land buyer must use the class that applies to the parcel.
A Capital Parcel Tax of $300 is collected with property taxes for Class 1, 8 and 9 properties in 2026, and drainage parcel taxes are also collected with property taxes.
The Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) taxable-area list includes the City of Surrey.

blocks.text: Surrey Lots and Land: getting around

items.t: Frequent bus stop areas are a planning fact, not just transit: lots within 400 metres of a stop with 15-minute service can qualify for 6 SSMUH units.

To check a project's servicing and permit status, the City's Online Development Inquiry shows rezoning, subdivision, development permit, engineering and building permit details by address or project number.

blocks.text: Surrey Lots and Land: risks and due diligence

items.t: Lowland land is near sea level because it was historically an intertidal zone, and both the Serpentine and Nicomekl are controlled by sea dams — flood construction is a lot-by-lot check.

The City has built dykes, pump stations and conveyance improvements in the agricultural lowlands since its 1997 Lowland Flood Control Strategic Plan, and states flooding has been significantly reduced — not eliminated.
Hazard lands can be exempt from SSMUH, and Steep Slope, Flood Plain, Sensitive Ecosystem and Farm Protection Development Permit Areas may require a development permit.
At application, the City requires the lot's own sewer, water and drainage servicing capacity to be considered for additional housing.

faq.a: On the City's own organization: a General Land Use Plan sets the overall framework for an area, a Neighbourhood Concept Plan provides the detailed neighbourhood plan under it, and a Local Area Plan does the same guiding work for areas planned outside the NCP process; approved plans are developed through community consultation and endorsed by Council, and they guide designations, density, roads, amenities and servicing.
faq.q: What is the difference between a GLUP, an NCP and an LAP in Surrey?

faq.a: No — Surrey City Centre is not a board name; the land is the Whalley sub-area. "City Centre" is the City of Surrey's planning name for its downtown, which is why the City Centre Plan tile legitimately uses it.
faq.q: Is "Surrey City Centre" a real estate board sub-area?

faq.a: One suite per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, never inside a coach house or garden suite, and never a separate strata lot. A "90 m² cap" is not the current rule.
faq.q: How big can a secondary suite be in Surrey?

faq.a: Not necessarily: the City records that the Surrey 2050 OCP update rescinded East Newton North and superseded the land use designations of East Newton South, the East Newton Business Park and West Cloverdale, with the OCP (Bylaw 21900) now guiding land use in those areas. Check the parcel's current OCP designation with the City before relying on any plan tile.
faq.q: If my lot is inside an NCP, is that plan still the operative one?

faq.a: Layers, in this order: the current OCP designation first, then the GLUP/NCP/LAP for the neighbourhood, then the current zoning under By-law No. 12000 — the plan shows where the City wants growth; the zoning is what can be built as-of-right today. Several tiles predate both the Surrey 2050 update and the July 8, 2024 SSMUH rezoning.
faq.q: In what order do I read a Surrey parcel?

faq.a: At subdivision approval or building permit issuance, not before approvals. The City's 2025 DCC report states the bylaw was amended so a DCC must be paid at approval of the subdivision or issue of the building permit, and developers may defer 75% until occupancy or within four years, whichever comes first.
faq.q: When are Development Cost Charges (DCCs) actually paid on a Surrey lot?

faq.a: Yes, as an additional unit, with caps. The City states the first SSMUH residential unit is exempt because DCCs were paid at original subdivision, additional units are charged by square footage at a rate comparable to townhouses, and garden and coach house DCCs are capped at 800 square feet.
faq.q: Does a garden suite or coach house attract its own DCC?

faq.a: The City's worked examples in its July 28, 2025 report put a duplex at $31,517.50 (down from $49,480.00 in the March bylaw) and a garden or coach house at $9,104 — City portion only, before Metro Vancouver and TransLink charges, and rates change by bylaw, so confirm the current schedule for your lot.
faq.q: How much is the DCC example the City itself publishes?

faq.a: No if it is over 4,050 m². Surrey states SSMUH applies to eligible residential lots under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary; 3 units are possible under 280 m², 4 units over 280 m², and 6 units only on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 metres of a frequent bus stop.
faq.q: Can a large Surrey lot use SSMUH for 4–6 units?

faq.a: New urban lots are created by subdivision against the parcel's zone minimum in Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000, and by added-unit development on existing lots, since Surrey's SSMUH framework allows 3 units on lots under 280 m², 4 units on larger lots and up to 6 on eligible lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop; on the agricultural edges, reserve land generally needs Agricultural Land Commission permission to subdivide.
faq.q: Where do buildable lots in Surrey come from?

faq.a: Only within tight limits: reserve land generally needs Agricultural Land Commission permission to subdivide, apart from limited approving-officer cases in the Agricultural Land Reserve General Regulation, and any new lot must also meet its Bylaw No. 12000 zone minimum.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a farm parcel in Surrey?

faq.a: A principal residence built without an Agricultural Land Commission application must be 500 m² or less in total floor area, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill for its construction, and a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence.
faq.q: How big a house can go on a reserve parcel?
